shelves.title: System Design
shelves.blurb: Active recall for interviews. Memorize the theory, the method, and the building blocks.

shelves.title: AI Engineering & Agents
shelves.blurb: Three books on building with foundation models: the engineering discipline, the agent patterns, and the multi-agent systems that compose them.

topics.title: Designing Data-Intensive Applications
topics.blurb: The distributed-data fundamentals: storage engines, replication, partitioning, transactions, consistency & consensus, batch & stream. The deep-dive theory interviewers probe.

topics.title: The System Design Interview
topics.blurb: How to actually run the interview: scope, structure, estimate, and drive — plus the back-of-envelope numbers every candidate should have memorized.

topics.title: Building Blocks
topics.blurb: The practical catalog DDIA omits: load balancers, caches, CDNs, message queues, rate limiters, and the scale primitives — the 'what do I reach for' vocabulary.

topics.title: Canonical Design Problems
topics.blurb: The classics — URL shortener, news feed, chat, rate limiter, Uber, Google Docs, payments, Ticketmaster, prescription marketplace. Each is an ordered walkthrough: requirements → estimation → API → architecture → deep dives → tradeoffs, drilled out loud.

topics.title: AI Engineering
topics.blurb: Building applications on top of foundation models: evaluation you can trust, prompting, RAG and agents, finetuning, dataset engineering, inference optimization, and the production architecture around them.

topics.title: Agentic Design Patterns
topics.blurb: The pattern catalog for agents — chaining, routing, parallelization, reflection, tool use, planning, memory, MCP, A2A, guardrails, evaluation. One named pattern per chapter, with the failure mode each one answers.

topics.title: Designing Multi-Agent Systems
topics.blurb: When one agent isn't enough: the multi-agent decision, orchestration topologies, agent UX, evaluation and optimization, and what it takes to run a crew of agents in production.
